feature: Copy a spec list or one measurement from the Measure menu
summary: The spec list and a single measurement's line can now be copied from the menu bar, and the spec list has a key. Plain command-C on a selected measurement also pastes as text in other apps.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. next-measure-panel is on by default. Open a screenshot and draw two or three measurements with the Measure tool (I).

try.do: Open the Measure menu in the menu bar. It now lists Copy as Spec List (control-command-C) and Copy Measurement between Measure Tool and Show All Measurements.
Press control-command-C, then paste into any text field. You get the header line and one line per visible measurement.
Click one measurement on the canvas, then choose Measure > Copy Measurement and paste. You get that one line, no header.
With the same measurement selected press plain command-C, then paste into a chat or a text editor. The same line appears; paste inside Photonz still lands a layer.
Marquee-select two measurements, open the Measure menu. The item reads Copy Measurements; choose it and paste to get both lines in panel order.
Turn a measurement's eye off in the Measurements panel, right-click its row, choose Copy Measurement. It still copies; Copy as Spec List leaves it out.
Delete every measurement. Copy as Spec List and Copy Measurement in the Measure menu are disabled.

evaluate: Is control-command-C a chord your hand finds, or would you rather Copy as Spec List sat on something else?
When you press it, do you trust that it worked? Nothing on screen confirms the copy.
Is plain command-C carrying the spec line as text a pleasant surprise or a confusion, for instance when you meant to paste the caliper somewhere else?
Should a hidden measurement copy when you explicitly pick it, or should the eye win everywhere?
Does Copy Measurement belong in the Measure menu, or would you look for it in Edit next to Copy?
rough: No confirmation after copying: the menu closes and nothing says the clipboard changed. Filed as a follow-up.
Copy Measurement has no chord of its own. Plain command-C already carries the line, and every free chord in the copy family needs three modifiers.
The Measurements panel has no click-to-multi-select; several measurements only select together through the canvas marquee.
The mock placed Copy measurement in a Properties panel menu Photonz does not have. It lives in the menu bar and in the row's context menu instead.
Verified by tests and a probe launch only: the loop cannot drive menus or take screenshots on this machine, so the menu was not clicked by hand.
